sections.html:
Go to the third floor of the Hertford County Courthouse, 119 Justice Drive, Suite 9, in Winton. The phone is 252-358-7850, and the office is open 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through Friday except county holidays and closings.

Staff keep real estate documents going back as far as 1862, and land deeds in the area date to 1710. The office holds deeds, deeds of trust, maps, military discharge records, notary records, and birth, death and marriage records for events in the county. Records are indexed by name, which is how a lawyer follows an old farm tract back through its owners.

The posted schedule warns that fees can change, so call before you send a check. Make checks payable to the Hertford County Register of Deeds and write a working phone number on them. For mailed returns, include your own stamped envelope addressed to yourself.

Real estate fees, Hertford County Register of Deeds
Document or servicePosted charge
Deeds and general instruments$26.00, first 15 pages; $4.00 per extra page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00, first 35 pages; $4.00 per extra page
Excise tax on deeds$2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price
Satisfactions and cancellationsNo fee
Non-standard document$25.00 per document
Several instruments in one packet$10.00 extra

Plat copies are $3.00 a page. Copy requests made by fax or online cost $1.00 for page one, then $.25 for each page after.

sections.h2: Formatting rules and the nonstandard fee
sections.html:
The recording rules repeat the paper standards of G.S. 161-14. A document that misses them is still recorded, with the $25.00 fee added.

  • Letter or legal size paper, one side only
  • Black type on white, 10 point or larger
  • Wide blank band across the head of page one

Session Law 2011-351 adds a drafter rule. Page one of a deed or deed of trust must name the person or law firm that prepared it. The county also wants the tax parcel pin on each deed, plus either a tax department stamp showing no delinquent taxes or a sentence directing the closing attorney to pay any back taxes from closing proceeds. Electronic deeds must carry the sentence.

Yes. Everything except maps can be e-recorded, and the e-recording page names Corporation Service Company and Simplifile as submitters. The recorded copy comes back electronically right after recording.

Your closing attorney picks the route, so a seller normally has nothing to submit personally.

If a document goes in on paper instead, mail it with a check payable to the Hertford County Register of Deeds, a working phone number, and a stamped envelope addressed to yourself for the return. Maps are the exception to e-recording and must be filed on paper.

sections.h2: What the office cannot do for a seller
sections.html:
Sellers often call the register for help it cannot give. Knowing the limits saves a trip.

  • It cannot search a title, because state law bars register staff from doing so. An individual or a legal representative can run the search.
  • It cannot confirm whether a lien exists. A deed of trust recorded in the office is the sign that the property secured a loan.
  • It cannot change a recorded deed. A new deed must be prepared, and the office recommends seeing an attorney.
  • It cannot name an owner from a street address, since records are indexed by name. Land Records Mapping, at 252-358-7809, handles location questions.
  • It holds no estate, will or divorce records. Those sit with the Clerk of Superior Court, 252-358-7100.

Real estate documents are online, though older indexes and images may not be.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax?
sections.html:
The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the burden on the transferor, and the county prints $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price on its schedule.

Under G.S. 47-18 a conveyance reaches later purchasers and lien creditors only once it is registered, so recording should follow signing quickly. The statutes are G.S. 105-228.30 and G.S. 47-18.

sections.h2: Other services at the Winton counter
sections.html:
The same office issues licenses and certificates. These may help if you also need paperwork for an estate or a move.

  • Certified birth, death or marriage copy: $10.00 each, with a government photo ID. Only close relatives or an authorized agent can pick one up.
  • Online vital record requests: $3.50 added, through the county's Get Certificate Now program.
  • Notary oath: $10.00. The Secretary of State sends the notice and no appointment is needed.
  • Military discharge filing and certified copy: free, though discharges are not open to public viewing.

The county had 19,015 people in mid 2025 and has 9,873 housing units. The median owned home is worth $119,200, and 67.4 percent of homes are owner occupied. Values are modest, so fixed charges such as recording fees weigh more on a small sale. Ask your closing attorney for the full list of closing costs before you set a price.

sections.h2: The 2027 revaluation and deeds recorded now
sections.html:
The county's revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, the first since 2019, and field measuring began in July 2025. Deeds recorded before and after that date follow the same recording steps. What changes is the assessed value attached to the parcel.

The Tax Assessor and Tax Collector sit at 115 Justice Drive in Winton. Ask the collector about the current bill before you close. The county also warns the public about deed scams, with a fraud detection page linked from the Register of Deeds site.

sections.h2: A seller's path through the office
sections.html:
Before closing, ask your attorney to confirm the deed will name you exactly as the record owner. A mistake means a new deed, since the office cannot change one already recorded. Check that page one names the preparer and carries the tax parcel pin, and that the deed includes the sentence directing back taxes to be paid from closing proceeds. Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff so no delinquent tax holds up the deed.

On closing day the seller's excise tax of $2.00 per $1000.00 is collected with the recording. Any paid-off deed of trust is cancelled at no fee. Recording is what protects the buyer against later purchasers and lien creditors, so ask the attorney to send the deed promptly. An e-recorded copy comes back electronically. A cash sale skips the lender's deed of trust, which means one fewer instrument to record and one less satisfaction to chase.

faqs.q: How much does Hertford County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The schedule lists $26.00 for a general instrument up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per extra page, and $64.00 for a deed of trust up to 35 pages. Call 252-358-7850 to check for changes.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax on a deed?
faqs.a: The county lists $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price, and the seller pays it.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed is formatted wrong?
faqs.a: It is recorded anyway, with a $25.00 non-standard fee added. Check the paper, type and page one rules above before you file.

faqs.q: Can staff search my title or find a lien?
faqs.a: No. State law keeps register staff from searching titles, and the office cannot confirm whether a lien exists. An attorney or title professional can read the recorded instruments.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of my recorded deed?
faqs.a: Yes, at the counter or on the county sites, though older indexes and images may be missing online. Certified copies are priced per page.
